# Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect — facts

> Source-anchored units about Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect: 15 across 4 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] Subscribe is a bidirectional, pull-based stream. The client grants event demand according to its processing capacity; this provides application-level flow control for a case-alert consumer. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://mi.docs.wso2.com/en/4.5.0/reference/connectors/sf-pubsub-inbound/sf-pubsub-inbound-endpoint-example/
- [statement] Additional FetchRequests add demand to undelivered demand on the existing stream. `pending_num_requested` reports events still owed to the client, so use it together with available processing capacity when deciding how much demand to replenish. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/flow-control.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] When `pending_num_requested` reaches zero, the client must send a new FetchRequest within 60 seconds of the last FetchResponse to keep the subscription stream open. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect
- [statement] When `pending_num_requested` is greater than zero but the event bus has no new events to deliver, the server sends an empty FetchResponse as a keepalive within 270 seconds. An empty response therefore does not by itself mean that the stream failed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api/blob/main/pubsub_api.proto

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Set `num_requested` to the number of events the consumer can accept. Salesforce documents a maximum request value of 100; the flow-control guide says requests above 100 are treated as 100. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/flow-control.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] An RPC error stops the long-lived subscription connection. The client must retry Subscribe to establish another connection; catching the exception alone does not continue delivery. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/handling-errors.html
- [statement] Salesforce recommends limiting retry attempts and using exponential backoff for long-lived RPC calls, with recovery behavior selected according to the received error. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/retry-rpc-calls.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect
- [statement] Inspect the custom error code in the gRPC exception trailers through `getTrailers()` to diagnose why the stream failed. Salesforce also supplies an RPC ID for support troubleshooting. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/retry-rpc-calls.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/handling-errors.html
- [statement] An RPC error terminates the long-lived Subscribe stream. The client must retry Subscribe to create a new stream; retry policy depends on the error, and Salesforce recommends limiting attempts and using exponential backoff for transient errors. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/retry-rpc-calls.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/handling-errors.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The Subscribe reference caps the `num_requested` field in FetchRequest at 100. Treat this as a documented request limit rather than a promise that an application can process that many concurrently. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect
- [statement] The pozil Node client exposes requestAdditionalEvents(topicName, numRequested) to add demand on an existing subscription; this is a client-library operation rather than a new RPC connection. (low confidence) — https://github.com/pozil/pub-sub-api-node-client · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect
- [statement] An Apache Camel issue reports that its PubSubApiClient could repeatedly resubscribe with an invalid replay ID, demonstrating why a reconnect loop must classify errors instead of blindly retrying identical input. (low confidence) — https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-21740 · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect
- [statement] FetchRequest and FetchResponse are not paired one-to-one: a requested event count can be delivered through multiple responses. Replenishment logic must track event capacity rather than assume one response completes one request. (high confidence) — https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api/blob/main/pubsub_api.proto · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://mi.docs.wso2.com/en/4.5.0/reference/connectors/sf-pubsub-inbound/sf-pubsub-inbound-endpoint-example/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A later FetchRequest must keep the original topic_name if it supplies one. A mismatch returns INVALID_ARGUMENT; changing the starting stream position requires a fresh Subscribe RPC. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://mi.docs.wso2.com/en/4.5.0/reference/connectors/sf-pubsub-inbound/sf-pubsub-inbound-endpoint-example/
- [statement] A Subscribe stream keeps one topic: a later FetchRequest may omit `topic_name`, but if present it must match the initial topic. A mismatch returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; changing the requested topic requires a separate subscription stream. (high confidence) — https://github.com/forcedotcom/pub-sub-api/blob/main/pubsub_api.proto · keywords: Salesforce Pub/Sub gRPC subscription flow control and reconnect · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
